aus-housing.extract:
Housing affordability in Australia is the ability for people to access housing in Australia through its property market or residential rental market. Housing in Australia’s major cities is among the least affordable in the world. Obtaining suitable housing has become increasingly out of reach as property prices have grown much faster than wages from the 2000s.
Since the 1990s, house prices have risen much faster than incomes. In June 2014, Australia had the third highest house price-to-income ratio in the world. In 2023, Australia experienced 8 consecutive quarters of house price rises, and 7 quarters of apartment price rises. From 1996 to 2024, the level of social housing construction did not keep pace with sales and demolitions of existing social housing stock.

cook-islands-dollar.title: Cook Islands dollar
hits: The Currency Reserves Amendment Act 1989 modified the required backing of Cook Islands dollars to 50% of the face value for circulating currency, and 2% of the face value for currency not intended for circulation (proof, uncirculated, and souvenir coin sets; uncut note sheets).
By 1993, circulating $3 notes were only backed by 5% of their face value in NZD, and coins were not backed at all.
In 1987, a smaller, lighter scallop-edged $1 coin with a similar size and shape to the Hong Kong $2 piece was issued.

With the release of its new $2 piece in that year, the Cook Islands became the first modern country to issue a circulating triangular coin, along with a dodecagonal (twelve-sided) $5 piece in equal size and shape to the Australian 50-cent coin.
These $1 and $2 were composed of cupro-nickel and the $5 coin was in aluminium bronze.
However, $1, $2, and $5 pieces remained in use.
cook-islands-dollar.extract:
The Cook Islands dollar is one of two current currencies of the Cook Islands, where it is used alongside the New Zealand dollar. The dollar is subdivided into 100 cents, with some older 50-cent coins carrying the denomination as "50 tene". 
Since 1995, the only valid Cook Islands banknote is the 3-dollar banknote; coins exist for 10, 20 and 50 cents, as well as for 1, 2 and 5 Cook Islands dollars.


== History ==
Until 1967, the New Zealand pound was used in the Cook Islands, when it was replaced by the New Zealand dollar.
In 1972, local issues of coins of the New Zealand dollar began to be released for the Cook Islands.
